name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (age >=12)
theme: the scan that removes a drug · Deauville checkpoint

meta.title: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adolescents and adults from age 12 - the S1826 trial deliberately unified those populations for advanced-stage disease. A young person's cancer with cure as the default expectation: the decisions are about HOW MUCH treatment, guided mid-course by the interim PET scan (Deauville), and about what the cure will cost in lungs, heart, fertility, and second cancers decades later. NLPHL is a DIFFERENT disease per WHO-HAEM5 (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma) - the histology gate reroutes it out.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the PET-adapted checkpoint archetype - the cancer where the mid-treatment scan can REMOVE a drug (RATHL: bleomycin out after a negative PET2, lungs spared, cure preserved), where the newest frontline standard (nivolumab-AVD) carries labeled PFS while its survival matures, and where the honest currency of every choice is measured in decades of survivorship.
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022): classic HL (CD30+) vs nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma (reclassified, CD20+); staging Ann Arbor/Lugano with early favorable/unfavorable/advanced grouping
meta.response: Lugano criteria with the Deauville 5-point PET scale - interim PET-CT is this disease's routing instrument (RATHL)

stages.label: Presentation & histology
stages.question: Classic Hodgkin - or its lymphocyte-predominant look-alike?
stages.decision: Excisional biopsy with expert hematopathology: CD30+ Reed-Sternberg cells define classic HL; CD20+ LP cells define a different disease (NLPBL) that reroutes ou…

stages.label: Stage & risk group
stages.question: Early favorable, early unfavorable, or advanced?
stages.decision: PET-CT staging (Lugano); risk-factor count (bulk, ESR, sites, B symptoms) splits early disease into favorable vs unfavorable; stage III-IV is advanced.

stages.label: Plan first-line therapy
stages.question: Early: combined modality at minimal dose. Advanced: which backbone - PET-adapted ABVD, Bv-AVD, or nivolumab-AVD?
stages.decision: Early favorable: 2xABVD + 20 Gy ISRT (HD10 noninferiority). Advanced: RATHL PET-adapted ABVD, Bv-AVD (mature 6-yr OS advantage), or N-AVD (best PFS, OS maturin…

stages.label: Interim PET checkpoint (Deauville)
stages.question: After 2 cycles: what does the scan give back - or demand?
stages.decision: PET2-negative on ABVD: drop bleomycin (RATHL - no loss of cure, fewer lung events). PET2-positive: escalate (BEACOPP per RATHL) and restage more often.

stages.label: Salvage & transplant fork (relapse)
stages.question: First relapse: salvage to autologous transplant - still the curative spine?
stages.decision: Salvage chemotherapy to PET-negative remission, then high-dose therapy + ASCT; brentuximab consolidation for high-risk remissions (AETHERA).

stages.label: Post-transplant / checkpoint era
stages.question: After (or instead of) transplant - what does PD-1 blockade change?
stages.decision: Pembrolizumab beat brentuximab head-to-head on PFS in relapsed/refractory disease (KEYNOTE-204); allogeneic transplant remains the late curative option for the…

stages.question: Which open randomized options exist for this profile?

stages.question: Which results are load-bearing for this plan?
stages.decision: Expert histology (CD30/CD20), staging PET-CT, risk-factor panel, interim PET with Deauville score, pulmonary function tests, fertility-preservation consult not…

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A young person's cancer with a second incidence peak past 55. The slider starts at 12 because S1826 did: adolescents and adults now share the advanced-stage evidence base.
Patient.helpPatient: Hodgkin lymphoma is most common in young adults - and the newest big trial treated teenagers and adults on one protocol, on purpose.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Older or frail patients carry more treatment risk - especially from bleomycin - and the guideline pathways adapt for them.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited. Most people with this disease start fit, and the plan means to keep them that way.

Patient.label: Pulmonary status
Patient.help: Bleomycin's lung toxicity is the classic ABVD hazard - impaired lungs close the bleomycin-containing cards and route toward the bleomycin-free programs (N-AVD, Bv-AVD) or the trial screen.
Patient.helpPatient: One of the classic drugs can scar lungs. If yours are already vulnerable, the plan starts from the bleomycin-free options instead.

Disease.label: Histology (expert hematopathology)
Disease.help: WHO-HAEM5 reclassified the lymphocyte-predominant form as nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-CELL LYMPHOMA - a different, indolent, rituximab-responsive disease. It reroutes to its own queued trainer.
Disease.helpPatient: Two diseases used to share the name 'Hodgkin'. The rarer, slower one now has its own name and its own playbook - this trainer hands it off rather than guessing.

Disease.label: Stage group (Lugano + risk factors)
Disease.help: PET-CT staging plus the risk-factor count (bulk, ESR, nodal sites, B symptoms). The stage group IS the menu - ranking waits for it.
Disease.helpPatient: Where the disease is and a few extra risk signs decide which of three very different plans applies. Worth the wait for the full scan.

On treatment.label: Interim PET after 2 cycles (Deauville)
On treatment.help: The routing instrument: negative on ABVD -> bleomycin comes OUT (RATHL: cure preserved, lungs spared); positive -> escalate and restage more often.
On treatment.helpPatient: The mid-treatment scan is not just a report card - a good scan literally removes a drug from your remaining treatment.

Relapse routing.label: Prior autologous transplant
Relapse routing.help: The relapse menu forks on this: transplant-naive relapse keeps the curative salvage-to-ASCT spine; post-transplant relapse routes to PD-1 blockade and, for the fit, the allogeneic question.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the 'own stem cells' transplant has already been used decides which doors are still open.

Relapse routing.label: Relapse pattern
Relapse routing.help: Primary refractory disease was AETHERA's highest-risk stratum - it raises the posterior and strengthens the consolidation case after transplant.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the disease never fully left, or came back later - the never-left pattern calls for the more reinforced plan.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: 2x ABVD + 20 Gy ISRT (early favorable; HD10 minimum)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN HL v1.2026 (combined modality, early stage)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: short chemotherapy exposure; the radiotherapy field is the long-term ledger (cardiac, breast, thyroid) - modern ISRT fields exist to shrink exactly that
Newly diagnosed.patient: For limited disease: two months of chemotherapy and a short course of focused radiation - one of the highest cure rates in oncology, proven with decades of follow-up.

Newly diagnosed.name: PET-adapted ABVD (RATHL - the scan that removes a drug)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the bleomycin question is designed OUT for most patients at the checkpoint; escalation toxicity is reserved for the scans that demand it
Newly diagnosed.patient: Start with the classic four-drug program; after two months a scan decides the rest - most people get to DROP the lung-toxic drug and keep the same cure.
drugs: ABVD -> AVD (bleomycin removed on negative interim PET)

Newly diagnosed.name: Brentuximab vedotin + AVD (ECHELON-1 - the mature OS win)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: febrile neutropenia (G-CSF prophylaxis required - the ECHELON-1 lesson) and peripheral neuropathy, mostly resolving; no bleomycin lung risk
Newly diagnosed.patient: The antibody-guided program that beat classic ABVD on survival itself at six years - and skips the lung-toxic drug entirely.

Newly diagnosed.name: Nivolumab + AVD (S1826 - the new standard, still maturing)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN HL v1.2026 (S1826-era option, advanced stage)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS primary met; OS immature
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: immune-related events (thyroid, rash, colitis) replace the antibody-drug conjugate's neuropathy; bleomycin-free
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest program: immunotherapy plus chemotherapy, with the best two-year disease control ever measured in this setting - and a card honest that the longest-term ledger is still being written.

Newly diagnosed.name: Supportive care only
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; B symptoms and progressive nodal disease dominate
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice, and in this disease the honest contrast is stark - the card shows it plainly so the choice is truly informed.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Salvage chemotherapy -> autologous transplant (the curative spine)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: standard of care + phase 3 consolidation evidence (AETHERA)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the transplant block is intense but time-boxed; consolidation adds neuropathy risk
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Relapse does not end curative intent: stronger chemotherapy to a clean scan, then the transplant - about half of patients are cured on this road.
drugs: Salvage chemotherapy (platinum- or Bv-based) -> high-dose carmustine-based conditioning + ASCT

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-204 - checkpoint era)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN HL v1.2026 (relapsed/refractory, post-ASCT or ineligible)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: immune-related events; pneumonitis is the one to respect in a chest-irradiated population
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: This disease is unusually visible to the immune system - the checkpoint drug beat the antibody-drug conjugate head-to-head at holding it back.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Allogeneic transplant (post-autologous failure, fit)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: GVHD and transplant-related mortality are real; checkpoint exposure before transplant needs a washout-and-vigilance plan (GVHD interaction)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The second, donor-based transplant - the late road to cure for fit patients whose own-cell transplant did not hold.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - a real chapter, chosen with real numbers.

milestones.title: Stage + interim-PET plan from the start
review: stage + favorable/unfavorable criteria pick the de-escalation lane (HD10: 2 cycles + 20 Gy suffices for the favorable, 10-year-proven)
the interim-PET plan is written BEFORE cycle one (RATHL: PET-negative drops bleomycin, PET-positive escalates - one scan, two roads)
advanced disease: N+AVD (S1826 PFS HR 0.45, better-tolerated) with ECHELON-1's OS-proven A+AVD as the alternative
fertility + survivorship planning at diagnosis - most patients are cured and live with the treatment, not the disease
